audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart said Level 1 was a skill stage and Levels 2-3 were Akali's. Both are backwards, and the two-item stage was given to Akali when the prose calls it even.
audit.why: Twofold Hex is 900 range against Five Point Strike's 550, and Akali has no Twilight Shroud until she can put a point in W — Level 1 is Aurora's outright. From 4-5 the shroud plus Shuriken Flip (16s at rank 1) let her pick the trade, and that Akali-sided middle runs through 6 and first item; at two items it flattens back to whoever lands first. The content whys already describe exactly this sequence, so only the enum sides were wrong. 46.15% over 182 games matches an Akali-sided middle.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Aurora / Skill / Skill / Akali / Akali / Akali / Skill, matching the packet chart, the mirror, and the existing whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named Aurora's ultimate "Between the Worlds" — no such ability — and never compared the two ultimate cooldowns, which is what actually decides the 6 spike.
audit.why: Riot's kit file names it Between Worlds (R) at 140/120/100 seconds. Perfect Execution is 120/90/60, so at rank 1 Akali gets her ultimate back 20 seconds sooner and the gap widens to 40 and 40 as they rank. Trading ultimate for ultimate is a losing exchange for Aurora at every rank.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (140s) zones her all-in, but Perfect Execution is 120s at rank 1 — she gets her ultimate back first, so never trade R for R.

audit.whatIsWrong: The pages describe Shuriken Flip only as a dash onto Aurora and describe Twilight Shroud loosely as "untargetable". They also assert repeatedly that Between Worlds makes Aurora untargetable from outside the rift, which is not in Riot's description of the ability.
audit.why: Shuriken Flip (E, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, 825 range): "The first enemy or smoke cloud hit is marked. Re-cast to dash to the marked target." She can mark her own Twilight Shroud and dash back into it — the shroud is an escape and a re-engage, not just cover, and that interaction is nowhere on the page. Twilight Shroud (W, 20/19/18/17/16, 350 range) makes her "invisible and unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks", but "Attacking or using abilities will briefly reveal her" — so the shroud is broken by her own aggression, which is the poke window. Assassin's Mark (P) is an auto-attack reset: exiting the energy ring empowers her next attack with bonus range, so her step-out is the tell, not her cast. Between Worlds' Riot text is a leap, a damaging slowing shockwave, and a zone that slows enemies inside and lets Aurora teleport across it — no untargetability anywhere.
audit.corrected: Shuriken Flip marks the first enemy or smoke cloud hit — she can E her own shroud and dash back in.

audit.whatIsWrong: No line gave the shroud's actual cooldown, so "poke when it is down" had no clock attached.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud is 20s at rank 1 and only 16s at rank 5, while Five Point Strike is a 1.5s energy cost — the shroud, not her Q, is the cooldown to count.
audit.corrected: Twilight Shroud is 20s at rank 1 — walk up only after she has spent it.

notes: Cross-cutting fabrication on Aurora's own pages, present in this matchup and most others in the slice: the text claims Between Worlds makes Aurora untargetable to enemies outside the rift. Riot's description contains no untargetability — only a leap, a damaging slowing shockwave, a slow zone, and a cross-zone teleport. Across the Veil grants invisibility, not untargetability. I did not assert the untargetability claim in any new text, but I have not rewritten every existing sentence that carries it (spikes[1], wants.you[1], mid, late here) because a correct replacement depends on whether the in-game zone really does grant it — logged in unverified. Akali's Twilight Shroud carries a revealsStealth derived flag; Riot's description only says attacking or casting reveals Akali herself, so whether the shroud reveals Aurora's Across the Veil invisibility is not established and I did not claim it.
